| NixOS VM | 按 `HACKING.md` 运行 `nix run .#checks.<system>.<test-name>.driver`，全部用 `nix flake check` | Nix，手动执行 | `nix/tests.nix` 定义的 GUI 与集成场景 | 非 NixOS 环境 |
| 上游 lint | 按 `HACKING.md`「Linting」一节运行 prettier、alejandra、shellcheck、swiftlint | 对应工具，本机均未安装 | 文档、Nix、shell、Swift 符合上游 lint 规则 | fork CI 不跑这些检查；没实际跑过就不能声称通过 |

聚合入口：`just framework-check` = rules-check → version-check → framework-test → kb-check → i18n-check → pinyin-check，不需要 Zig，本机约 15 s；`just ci-check` = framework-check → fmt-check → test-vt，提交前必跑，热缓存约 100 s，改过 Zig 源码另加约 2 min 编译（见下节）；`just generated-check` = kb-check → i18n-check → pinyin-check → graph-check，上游同步后与发版前必跑。valgrind、fuzz、esctest、benchmark、NixOS VM 与上游 lint 是上游的手动流程，fork 不提供专门的 just 配方，也不进 CI。

示例、`test/fuzz-libghostty` 与 `test/esctest` 是各带 `build.zig` 的子工程，`just` 配方总在仓库根执行、进不了这些目录；表中子工程里的 `zig build …` 都在该目录用钉版 Zig 运行，即 `python ../../scripts/zigw.py build …`（Linux/macOS 用 `python3`）。

## Windows GUI 验证

本机 Windows 能直接运行 Ghostty GX，GUI 可见的 Windows 改动在本机验收（规则正文在 `docs/AGENT_RULES/apprt-win32.md`「验证」段）；GTK 走 WSL 的 `just wsl smoke` 或 `gx-ci` 的 `gtk-smoke`，macOS 没有 GUI 冒烟。

做法：

1. 构建：`just build`；看性能或发布形态时用 `-Doptimize=ReleaseFast`，或解压 `just package-windows` 的便携 zip。
2. 隔离：把 `LOCALAPPDATA` 与 `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` 都指向 `.local/evidence/<任务>/env/<场景>`，配置写在其下的 `ghostty\config.ghostty`，日志落在 `ghostty\logs\ghostty.log`，不读写用户真实的配置与日志。隔离后，只装在真实 `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs` 下、不在 `PATH` 上的 GX Zsh 探测不到，默认 shell 会退到 PowerShell，需要时在配置里写 `command`。agent 的 shell 常带 `NO_COLOR=1`，启动前去掉它，否则 pwsh 等不输出颜色与粗斜体。`just win-gui` 自动做这些隔离。
3. 操作：优先用 `just win-gui`（见下文）回放场景或逐条发命令；临时探查也可用其他桌面自动化（如 kimi-cu 对 `GhosttyWindow` 的截图、点击与按键），或 PowerShell 的 `CopyFromScreen` 截图脚本。执行要验证的操作：点击、按键、输入法输入、拖动改尺寸、切换语言或主题等。
4. 截图与读图：在每个要证明的状态截图，图片存到 `.local/evidence/<任务>/`（gitignored，不入库），逐张打开读图、对照预期写结论；同时读日志里相关的行（如 `loaded OpenGL … software=`、`ConPTY: …`、确认与菜单的日志）。结论写明提交、构建类型、Windows 版本号、显示缩放、显卡或 Mesa（日志里的 `renderer=` 与 `software=`）。

可以记 PASS 的证据：在真实桌面会话里截下、已经读过、能看出预期状态的截图，加上对应的日志行。不能记 PASS 的：只确认进程在运行或窗口存在；截图全黑、全白或截到了别的窗口；截了但没读；只读日志没看界面。

已知的坑：微软拼音把 Ctrl+Shift+F 当作简繁切换吞掉，自动化测试查找栏前先切到英文键盘布局，或从命令面板打开查找；GUI 子系统的 exe 没有控制台（见下文「Windows 本机限制」）；复现 CI 的软件渲染设 `GHOSTTY_GX_OPENGL=software`，并把 Mesa 的 DLL 放进 exe 旁的 `mesa\`。

## 耗时度量与基线

`scripts/gx_perf.py`（`just perf`）收集、汇总并对比 GUI 的耗时样本，只管测量与统计；结论要写明机器、构建类型与负载。

- **样本**：`src/gx/perf.zig::record` 只写微秒时间 `info(gx_perf): <指标> <值>us`；解析器兼容 ns、ms、s 的历史时间行。计数必须另用无单位的 `metric <名> <值>`，同名 time/count 冲突拒绝。另收集 `metric <名> <值> [s|ms|us]`、Debug 的 `window shown after <n>ms`、`gx_win_gui.py` 的 `startup_ms`，以及 Windows 时间戳日志里的首次 OpenGL 探测、配置、字体、子进程与渲染上下文里程碑。时间换算为毫秒，p90 取最近秩；递归路径归一去重，父子目录重叠不会增加 n，跳过隔离配置目录中的日志原件。普通 `summarize` 仍可汇总任意指标，但不是性能通过门。
- **Windows**：`just perf win32 --exe <旧> --exe <新> --out <目录> [--runs 10] [--resizes 6] [--env 名=值]`。每个构建一个隔离配置，先跑一轮丢弃的预热，此后都是热启动；两个构建按 A B、B A 交替，让机器状态的漂移同时作用于两边。每轮记录进程创建到主窗口创建、可见、取消 cloak 的时间（`startup.created`、`startup.visible`、`startup.shown`，1 ms 轮询），Ctrl+Shift+T 与 Ctrl+Shift+O 到新终端子窗口可见的时间（`new_tab.terminal_visible`、`split.terminal_visible`），`SetWindowPos` 改尺寸的同步耗时（`resize.setwindowpos`），以及窗口是否仍响应消息。每轮写 `<目录>/<标签>/run-NN.txt` 与日志副本，最后写 `SUMMARY.txt`。
- **GTK**：先 `just wsl build --gtk -Doptimize=ReleaseFast`，再 `just perf gtk --clone <克隆> [--clone <克隆>] --out <新目录> [--runs 10] [--env 名=值]`。GTK 没有自动预热；默认 AB/BA 各 10 轮，每轮都是新的私有配置和 Xvfb 会话。正常负载仍是 `seq 1 3000000`，不缩样本、不补跑失败轮。窗口出现及 done 文件都每 50 ms 轮询；elapsed 是 realtime 差，超时用 monotonic；CPU 窗口含结束后的 1 秒排空尾巴，不是与 workload_seconds 完全相同的区间。DMABUF 警告按匹配行计数，一行多个关键词只计一次。`llvmpipe-N` 合组，实际出现但未耗 CPU 的线程组仍记零；缺失不补零。
测试与证据（gx_ghostty） > 耗时度量与基线

- **GTK 有效性**：实际 held exe 的 `+version` 验证 ReleaseFast，普通非 perf GUI smoke 仍可用 Debug。性能前先精确提交源树，经正常 `just wsl build --gtk -Doptimize=ReleaseFast` 生成 `.local/gx-wsl/gtk-build-receipt.json`（`gx-gtk-build-v1`）：构建 argv/退出、构建前后 commit/tree/dirty、实际 exe SHA/版本。argv 按钉版 Zig 0.16 `lib/compiler/build_runner.zig` 的选项消耗方式分类：默认目标或唯一 `install` 才能签收；允许 `--summary all`、`--color off` 等已登记带值选项及 `-j4`。该版本 `-j 4` 实测为 InvalidCharacter，不替使用者偷偷改写。`gx_wsl.py --help` 显示工具帮助，`gx_wsl.py build --help/-h` 则进入正常 Zig query，不被子命令 argparse 提前截走。help/list、test/custom step、`--`、prefix/target/emit、skip-oom 或未知 flag 都不签收性能；普通命令仍透传 Zig 输出/退出，即使查询退出 0，receipt 也只有 ineligible attempt，不探测旧映像。脏树、源树变化及不符的 version override 同样拒绝；不能手写 receipt 代 build。smoke 与 collector 交叉核对 receipt、实际映像身份、原始 version/version_exit、干净源树及 cleanup/child_exit。正常受控 pidfd SIGTERM 后 child_exit 为 -15（或正常 0）允许，崩溃 -11 等拒绝。
- **进程与线程**：启动、采样前后、xdotool、清理核对 PID/字段 22/实际 exe；持有未回收直接 Popen child 与 pidfd，信号只发受控 pidfd。pidfd 不可用启动前拒绝；打开失败只清自己的未回收 child。端点 TID/字段 22、统计完整性、负增量、main/renderer、负载/退出继续严格守门；两端相同不证明窗口内没有线程出生/退出。
测试与证据（gx_ghostty） > 耗时度量与基线

- **CPU 观测与诊断**：每个端点用 `/proc/<pid>/stat` 前后夹住 task 遍历，保存原始 stat 与 monotonic ns 的读序/持续时间。`cpu.total` 取进程 post_stat 的累计 tick 增量（真实短线程试验证实包含已退出线程）；`cpu.endpoint_threads` 与各组是端点仍存活线程的量化计数，不保证相加等于进程 total。旧样本进程 1611 与端点 1571、残差 U/S=16/24、候选界 284 仅是观测，不证明 Linux adjusted CPU counters 的舍入逻辑满足 `n_before+n_after+2`。该公式及夹读增长只保留为 `diagnostic_only` 的候选界，明确 proof=unproved；不再用 `comparable=True`、超界或 50 ms 候选预算决定样本有效性，也不把残差说成精确 transient CPU/未归属区间。source identity、稳定 TID birth、完整 workload、计数非负和合法读序仍 fail-closed。比较仅在相同声明时钟/负载/环境及完整计划下统计这些观测 tick，不保证全人口、精确计量或优化收益。零组与原 comm 保存，token 碰撞拒绝。
- **证据合同**：保存 `*-meta.json`（`gx-gtk-perf-v1`）、唯一 capture_id、raw tasks/process/status/times、build receipt、退出/finished、身份检查点、实际软件相关环境与制品哈希；collector 从 raw 重算对账与 metric，不只信 valid/errors。同名前缀在排他锁内复查，复制使用独占创建，冲突非零且保留未复制 raw。GTK out 必须新/空；`gtk-runs.json` 核对唯一 `(label,run,path)`、完整 canonical AB/BA 顺序、路径不逃出 owned out、不经 symlink、每轮实际 manifest SHA 和唯一 capture。`RESULT.json` 保留原 planned_runs 与失败原因，不补跑缩 n。渲染日志保留，但 Xvfb/Mesa/env 不证明 EGL/硬件/CPU fallback，未知为 unknown。
- **对比**：`just perf compare --old <目录或文件…> --new <目录或文件…>` 要求指标/单位类别/n 对齐；GTK 两侧各有 runs 个 main/renderer/total 和窗口/负载时间。来自 declared batch 的选择还必须包含每个选中 label 的全部 planned_runs 原件；声明 10 轮却各选 run-01 不能因 n=1,1 变绿。历史无 manifest timing 可继续 unverified 统计，但旧合格身份、不完整新 receipt/CPU 对账均不能代新合同。单个 smoke 的验证只证明 harness/source 证据，不代新旧各 10 次性能门；不内置收益百分比，性能结论仍需同机同时间段 AB/BA。

## 并行运行器与耗时

用户要求所有测试不超过 2 分钟；本机热缓存曾测得 95–110 s，但不保证每轮达标：后续包含 544 个框架测试的 `just ci-check` 实测 133.52 s（框架 12.79 s，test-vt 118.0 s，其中构建 1.5 s），退出 0、6593 条 Zig 用例通过、62 条跳过，性能要求未达成。冷编译、源码变更后的重编译与完整 CI 同样尚未达成要求。不能排除编译耗时或缩小覆盖后宣布目标完成。下列历史热缓存结果只说明其声明条件下的耗时，命令参数与退出码见 MAKE_COMMANDS.md。

**原理**：上游 `zig build test-lib-vt` 与 `zig build test` 让每个测试二进制在一个进程里逐条运行，多核基本闲置。fork 补丁 GX-0002 新增只编译、安装而不运行的步骤 `test-lib-vt-bin` 与 `test-bin`（见 FORK_PATCHES.md），`scripts/zig_test.py` 再按 Zig 测试运行器的 server 协议（`--listen=-`：先 `query_test_metadata` 取用例名，再逐条 `run_test`）把用例分到多个进程。全部用例排成一张任务表，按 `.local/test-timings/<label>.json`（`GX_ZIG_TEST_TIMINGS_DIR` 可换目录）从长到短分给 `--jobs` 个工作线程，每个线程对每个二进制复用一个测试进程；没有记录的用例按 0.1 s 估计，删掉缓存只改变调度顺序，不改变结论。每轮运行后把实测并入缓存；只有本轮由 `--suite` 构建、且 `-D` 与 `--zig-arg` 里都没有 `-Dtest-filter` 的完整二进制，才顺带删去二进制里已不存在的用例，`--no-build`、`--binary` 与带 `-Dtest-filter` 的运行只合并不删。用例崩溃或超时（单条默认 600 s）后，运行器为剩余用例重启进程。超时、崩溃与中断时，运行器在 POSIX 上杀掉测试进程所在的整个进程组，Windows 上在超时与中断时杀掉整个进程树；中断指 Ctrl+C，POSIX 上还包括 SIGTERM、SIGHUP，清理后退出 130（`scripts/run_unittests.py` 对 SIGTERM、SIGHUP 的处理相同）。

**判定**与 `zig build` 相同（`std/Build/Step/Run.zig::evalZigTest`）：先看 fail，再看内存泄漏（leak）与 error 日志（log_err）；skip 单列、不算失败；崩溃、超时与未运行都算失败。随机种子默认每轮随机，结论行总会打印 `seed 0x…`；有失败时还会打印一条可直接复制执行的复现命令：`python scripts/zig_test.py`，带上本次的 `--suite`/`--binary`、`-D`、`--zig-arg`、`--no-build` 与非默认的 `--timeout`，再加 `--seed 0x…` 与引好的 `--filter <用例全名>`。用例全名含空格，复现时原样执行这条命令，不经 just。怀疑运行器本身（分片、进程复用、执行顺序）影响结论时，用上表的上游串行路径对照。

**框架单测**：`scripts/run_unittests.py` 把每个 `TestCase` 类作为一个单元放进独立子进程，并发默认取逻辑核数与 8 的较小值——这些单元主要在起 git、bash、PowerShell 与 Python 子进程，Windows 上进程创建在少量并发时就饱和，再多只会互相拖慢。调度按 `.local/test-timings/unittest.json` 从慢到快，`RUN_LAST = True` 的类在其余单元全部启动后才启动（`scripts/test_ai_tool_hooks.py::WindowsEntryTests` 启动 Windows PowerShell 5.1，与其他单元同时跑会拖慢整机的进程创建）。子进程跑的测试数与发现阶段不符也记失败。

- **下限**：各用例耗时合计约 1600 s（20 路并行下测得），1600 / 20 ≈ 80 s，所以 80 s 已接近 20 核的下限；最慢的单条用例 `terminal.Terminal.test.Terminal: printSlice differential fuzz vs print` 本机约 39–58 s，核数再多也快不过它。笔记本 CPU 连续满载后会降频：上表第二次紧接着第一次运行，test-vt 多花了约 10 s；本机同时有其他重负载时，全量可能超过 2 分钟。
- **`--dedupe`** 是覆盖取舍：vt_c 是同一模块以 `c_abi = true` 编译的测试二进制，同名用例在 C ABI 打开时再跑一遍，另有只在它里面的 `terminal.c.*`；去重后少了 C ABI 打开时的那一遍。默认关闭；用了就在结论里写明。
- **编译**：改过 Zig 源码后，`ghostty-vt`、`ghostty-vt-c` 两个 Debug 测试二进制都要用 LLVM 重新编译，两次编译并行，各约 2 min、约 6 GB 内存（RSS）。这段时间运行器省不掉：试过 Zig 自托管后端，它在 Windows 上编出的测试二进制无法运行。没改 Zig 源码时，`test-lib-vt-bin` 只做 1 秒内的缓存校验；运行器给测试构建钉 `-Dversion-string=<X.Y.Z>-dev+0000000`，否则版本串随提交哈希变化，每次提交都会让测试二进制整体重编。
- **CI**：`gx-ci` 的托管 runner 只有 4 个 vCPU，LLVM 编译测试二进制本身就要数分钟，用例也只能分 4 路，已测 CI 未达到 2 分钟。旧布局首次运行墙钟约 22 min（旧 `linux` job 21.5 min、`windows` 19 min）。新布局把 Linux 拆成并行的 `linux-vt` 与 `linux-main` 并改用运行器，2026-10-07 首次运行（run 37582059213，冷缓存、没有耗时记录）墙钟约 14.4 min：`linux-vt` 9.5 min（构建 91 s，6651 条用例 429 s）、`linux-main` 12.8 min（构建 419 s，3909 条用例 330 s）、`windows` 13.9 min（构建 304 s，6655 条用例 323 s），`lib-vt-cross` 各 1.3–2.7 min。之后加入的 `windows-app` 还没有在 GitHub 上跑过。

### CI 缓存诊断

`mlugg/setup-zig` 跨运行保存的 Zig 缓存目录超过 `cache-size-limit` 就被清空。旧 `linux` job 约 2.99 GB 超过默认 2048 MiB；三个测试 job 提高到 4096 MiB 后仍有失效：2026-10-07 run 37587736223 的 `linux-vt` 最终为 **5,078,327,232 字节**，超过 4096 MiB 被清空，下一轮恢复的只有 **186 字节**。不能把恢复步骤成功视为有效热缓存命中。

钉版 translate-c 源码已证实 `--zig-lib` 参数的路径直接进入 hash，旧 setup-zig 的随机解压路径因而会改变输入。后续两轮已观测到两个 VT job 的 CPU 型号变化，但其与 miss 的因果关系不能一概而论，见下方实测。当前实现与验收边界：

- `linux-vt`、`linux-main`、`windows` 的 setup-zig 均设 `use-tool-cache: true`，以固定工具链路径减少路径变体，并用 `cache-key: stable-toolchain-v1` 隔离旧变体；不删除旧 cache，4096 MiB 上限不变。`windows-app` 用同一组设置。`lib-vt-cross` 仍按 target 分 key。
- 三个测试 job 的 `GX_ZIG_TEST_TIMINGS_DIR=.zig-cache/gx-test-timings` 让调度记录随 Zig 缓存保存；只有真正恢复到有效记录，才可按上轮耗时调度。构建增加 `--summary all`（经运行器 `--zig-arg` 透传），从日志区分缓存命中和实际编译。
- `scripts/ci_cache.py snapshot` 在 restored 与 finished 两阶段按白名单记录 CPU 型号/核数、Zig 可执行文件与库路径、local/global cache 总量及顶层分区大小、timings 条数；不导出完整环境变量或文件内容。报告里的不完整扫描或错误不能当作完整统计。
- 手动输入 `cache_probe` 默认 false，只有 `workflow_dispatch` 且为 true 时才在同一 runner 重复相同套件的安装构建（main 保留 `-Dapp-runtime=none`），不重复运行用例；普通 push/PR 不增加这次编译。probe JSON 记录命令、耗时与退出码，详细构建 summary 在 job 日志。
- `gx-zig-test-<job>` 以 `always()` 上传测试 JSON、`cache-restored.json`、`cache-finished.json` 和启用探针时的 `cache-probe.json`，保留 14 天。finished 快照在 setup-zig 的 action post 之前，只反映保存前状态；还要检查 post 日志是否超限清空、下一轮 restored 是否恢复了有效数据。

- **跨 runner 仅部分复用。** 第二轮首次构建仍有 translate-c 与测试编译节点未 cached；缓存 `o` 分区继续增长，不能把恢复成功或同机全 cached 写成跨运行全命中。本次结束大小虽均低于 4096 MiB，未来仍可能超限，不能宣称所有缓存问题已解决。

固定路径、缓存恢复、timings 保留和同机快速复建已验收；跨 runner 完整复用及增长控制仍需后续运行补证。「所有测试 ≤2 min」仍未达成，不能用 probe 秒数替代全量耗时，也不得删用例、默认去重或收窄覆盖。

## CI 覆盖与本机对应

`gx-ci.yml` 的触发：push 到 `gx_ghostty`、目标为 `gx_ghostty` 的 PR，以及手动 `workflow_dispatch`（可选输入 `gtk_smoke`、`win_smoke`、`macos`、`cache_probe`，均默认 false）。全局只有 `contents: read` 权限；同一 PR 的新运行会取消旧运行，push 与手动运行互不取消（每次 push 的提交标题都要校验）。`framework` 与 `zig-fmt` 并行先跑，其余 job 都等它们通过。CI 用 `mlugg/setup-zig` 把 Zig 放到 PATH 上：直接写的 `zig build …` 用它；两个运行器经 `scripts/zigw.py` 调用 Zig，zigw 在没有钉版目录时回退到 PATH 上的同一个 Zig（版本仍须等于 `scripts/setup_zig.py::ZIG_VERSION`）。

| job | 何时运行 | 内容 | 本机对应 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `framework` | 每次 | resolver `--check`、version `--check`、`python3 scripts/run_unittests.py`、kb-check、首父链提交标题校验（push 取 `before..after`，`before` 全零时只查 head；PR 取 `base..head`；手动触发只查 head）；不跑 graph-check 与 i18n-check（GX 译表由框架单测里的 `scripts/test_gx_i18n.py` 校验） | `just framework-check`；`just commit-check --range <base>..HEAD` |

## Windows 本机限制

能跑：框架单测、`just fmt-check`、`just test-vt` 与 `just build-vt`（MSVC）、`just build` 与 `just test`（GNU ABI，win32 apprt）、Windows GUI 验证、`just package-windows`，以及经 `just wsl` 的 Linux 构建、单测与 Xvfb 截图。限制与已知的环境性失败：

- **GTK 与 macOS 的 GUI**：本机没有，GTK 用 WSL 的 `smoke` 或 `gx-ci` 的 `gtk-smoke` 补证；macOS 只能用 `gx-ci` 的 `macos`（lib-vt 测试）或 `gx-release` 的 macOS 构建补证构建层面，GUI 行为记 PENDING，不记 N/A（能力存在、只是本机缺环境）。
- **只在 Linux 上编译的代码**：`/proc`、`tcgetpgrp` 分支与 GTK apprt 不进 Windows 的 `ghostty-test`，用 `just wsl test`（`--gtk` 带上 GTK apprt）或 `gx-ci` 的 `linux-main` 补证。
- **MSVC ABI 与嵌入库**：lib-vt 走 MSVC；不经 `just` 时 Windows 目标默认也是 MSVC，app 与 `ghostty-test` 在 MSVC 下能否编译未验证。`-Dapp-runtime=none` 的 libghostty-internal 在 Windows 上链接失败（缺 `gladLoadGLContext` 等符号，见 `docs/AGENT_RULES/build-system.md`「平台」），Windows 上没有可用的嵌入库；上游手测程序 `test/windows/test_dll_init.c` 要先编出 `ghostty-internal.dll`（步骤见 `test/windows/README.md`），因此仍无法执行，记 PENDING 并注明受阻。
- **符号链接权限**：`src/lib/tinyio` 的 `deleteFile edge cases` 与 `windows: realPath resolves through symlinks` 要创建符号链接。未开启开发者模式（也不是管理员）时它们以 `PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD` → `PermissionDenied` 失败：`just test-vt` 里每个用例在两个测试二进制各失败一次，共 4 处；`just test` 里各一次，共 2 处。这是环境前置不满足，不是代码回归；记 FAIL 并注明原因，开启开发者模式后重跑，不跳过、不改用例。gx-ci 的托管 runner 有管理员令牌：`windows` job 的 `--suite vt` 与 `windows-app` 的 `--filter lib.tinyio` 跑到这 6 处，可作 CI 补证，但不覆盖本机记录的 FAIL。
- **i18n**：Windows 上 `zig build update-translations` 直接报错（构建脚本在 gettext i18n 关闭时拒绝该步骤），上游 pot 与 `.po` 的检查交给 Linux；GX 译表 `just i18n-check` 本机照常可跑。
测试与证据（gx_ghostty） > Windows 本机限制

- **`test-lib-vt-schema`**：`build.zig` 用 `python3` 执行 `src/terminal/c/types-schema-verify.py`，缺 `jsonschema` 时脚本以「run this inside `nix develop`」退出。框架不代装这个依赖，缺失时记 PENDING，由 `gx-ci` 的 `linux-vt` job 补证。
- **GUI 子系统程序的输出**：`ghostty.exe` 没有控制台，`+version`、`+list-fonts`、`+show-config` 等只在标准输出被重定向或接管道时可见；PowerShell 里要 `| Out-String`，赋值给变量或 `>` 会遇到 `PIPE_CLOSING`。
- **崩溃退出码**：Git Bash 与 `zig build run` 会把 Windows 进程的 NTSTATUS 截成 8 位。要看原生程序的真实崩溃码，在 pwsh 里直接运行程序并读 `$LASTEXITCODE`（上游 Windows job 的做法）；`scripts/zig_test.py` 记 crash 时打印完整的 32 位退出码（如 `0xC0000005`）。
- **graphify**：Windows 智能应用控制会拦截 venv 里生成的未签名 `graphify.exe`（WinError 4551），`scripts/graphify.py` 因此一律用 `python -m graphify`。
- valgrind 与 AFL++ 只在 Linux、macOS 上可用；Nix VM 测试需要 Nix。

**WSL**：装有 WSL2 时，`just wsl` 在 WSL 克隆里补跑完整单测、GTK 构建与 Xvfb 截图（分层表「WSL 本机 Linux」）。2026-10-09 在 32 逻辑核的 WSL Ubuntu 24.04 上实测：`just wsl setup` 从零（克隆、钉版 Zig、blueprint-compiler、39 个 Zig 包）85 s，已就绪时约 1 s；GTK Debug 冷构建 69 s；主套件 3939 条（3897 通过、42 跳过）冷编译时墙钟 267 s（构建 225 s），热缓存 43 s；`just wsl test --gtk` 带上 GTK apprt 共 3971 条（3929 通过、42 跳过），冷编译时墙钟 306 s（构建 231 s）；lib-vt 6712 条（6642 通过、70 跳过）热缓存 84 s；`smoke` 约 25 s（含默认 20 s 等待）。这些数字测于 `src/gx/`、win32 apprt 与 GTK 的 GX 层合入之前，现在的用例数更多。WSL 的限制：Xvfb 里没有窗口管理器与合成器，截图只证明 X11 下的软件渲染；WSLg 窗口内容截不到；Zig 自己的下载走不了 HTTP 代理（`gx_wsl.py` 用 curl 预取绕开）。WSL 结果是本机 Linux 证据，不代证 `gx-ci` 的 `linux-main` 与 `gtk-smoke`，GUI 可见变更的 PASS 判据不变。

## 故障注入预期

关键门必须被证明「会失败」。注入只在临时副本或临时输入上做：框架单测用临时目录；需要完整仓库时在 `.local/tmp/` 下建临时 clone。不要修改跟踪中的文件再事后还原。

| 注入 | 应失败的门 | 预期 |
|---|---|---|
| 新增一个没有路由覆盖的文件 | `just rules-check` | 退出 2，列出未覆盖文件 |
| 新增一份嵌套 `AGENTS.md` | `just rules-check` | 退出 2，指出实际集合与 `nested_agents` 不一致 |
| 改动 KB 语料（文档、公开签名、文档注释）但不重建 | `just kb-check` | 退出 1，列出变化来源；只改函数体时仍为 0 |
| 改 `.po` 但不重建 GX 译表 | `just i18n-check` | 退出 1 |
| 改动被索引源码但不重建图谱 | `just graph-check` | 退出 2；改动被 `.graphifyignore` 排除的文件时仍为 0 |
| `CHANGELOG.md` 标题格式错误或版本重复 | `just version-check` | 退出 1 |
| 在 `.github/workflows/` 放回一个上游 workflow | `scripts/test_gx_workflows.py`（`just framework-test` 内） | 失败 |
| 删掉 fork 补丁标记 | `scripts/test_fork_patches.py`（`just framework-test` 内） | 失败 |
| 不合规的提交信息 | `python scripts/conventional_commits.py "<标题>"`、`just commit-check --message-file <文件>`、commit-msg hook | 退出 1，hook 拒绝提交 |
| KB 乱码查询 | `scripts/test_agent_kb.py` 的检索回归（`just framework-test` 内） | 返回空结果；正常的中英文查询命中预期文档 |
| 危险命令，如 force push | hook 探针 `scripts/test_ai_tool_hooks.py` | 真执行被拒；只是文本提及（如出现在提交信息里）则放行 |
| 找不到 Zig | 经 `scripts/zigw.py` 的配方，如 `just test-vt` | 退出 2，提示运行 `just setup` |
| `--filter` 写了不存在的子串 | `just test-vt --filter <不存在的子串>` | 退出 2，报「运行期 --filter … 没有匹配任何用例」，不会一条都没跑也报绿 |
| `-Dtest-filter` 写了不存在的子串 | `just test-vt -Dtest-filter=<不存在的子串>`（会重编两个测试二进制） | 退出 2，报「构建期 -Dtest-filter=… 裁掉了全部用例」；之后 `--no-build` 再跑这批被裁空的二进制，报「测试二进制本身没有用例」 |

## 证据规则

| 结论 | 条件 |
|---|---|
| PASS | 命令在声明的环境里实际跑完、退出码为 0，并能给出命令、提交、环境与输出位置；截图类验收还必须实际读过图 |
| FAIL | 实际跑了，但退出码非 0 或断言失败。保留输出，修复后复测，不覆盖失败记录 |
| PENDING | 需要验证但当前环境跑不了，例如本机没有 GTK 或 macOS 桌面、提交还没 push、CI 尚未首跑、客户端未安装。必须写明原因与补验命令 |
| N/A | 该能力本项目不存在，例如项目没有内置 AI，RuleManifest 记 N/A。必须写明理由，不能拿来掩盖缺环境 |

- 以退出码判定，不凭输出「看起来成功」。验收命令不接会吞退出码的管道：不写 `just test-vt | tail`、`| head`。需要留存输出时重定向到文件，再检查退出码：
  - Git Bash：`just test-vt > .local/test-vt.log 2>&1; echo $?`
  - PowerShell：每条原生命令后立即检查 `$LASTEXITCODE`，别让后一条的成功覆盖前一条的失败
  - cmd：`echo %ERRORLEVEL%`
- 定向测试要报告 filter 字符串、seed 和实际运行的用例数（运行器计数表的 `total` 列）。运行器零命中时退出 2，报错写明是运行期 `--filter` 没命中还是构建期 `-Dtest-filter` 裁掉了全部用例；走上游 `zig build` 路径时，filter 拼错可能一个测试都没跑也照样退出 0，所以要加 `--summary all` 核对，例如 `just zig build test-lib-vt -Dtest-filter=<名> --summary all`。
- 运行器的结论还要写明非默认参数：`--dedupe`、`--serial-filter`、`--jobs`、`--timeout`。需要留存结果时可加 `--json <文件>`（schema 见 `scripts/zig_test.py::build_report`）。
- 截图类结论写明截图的来源（本机桌面、WSL 的 Xvfb、CI artifact 名与 run）、读图结论与对应的日志行；Windows GUI 的具体要求见上文「Windows GUI 验证」。
- 一层通过不证明另一层：test-vt 通过不等于完整单测通过；Windows 的 `just test` 通过不等于 Linux 的 `linux-main` 通过；交叉编译通过不等于该目标上能运行；WSL 截图不等于 `gtk-smoke` 截图；artifact 存在不等于截图验收通过。
- 必要工具缺失时，不得整族跳过后报绿，记 PENDING。
- CI 结论要引用具体运行：workflow、run、job 与提交 SHA。本地 `actionlint` 只证明 workflow 语法，不证明 job 能通过。

# Example Libghostty Projects

Each example is a standalone project with its own `build.zig`,
`build.zig.zon`, `README.md`, and `src/main.c` (or `.zig`). Examples are
auto-discovered by CI via `example/*/build.zig.zon`, so no workflow file
edits are needed when adding a new example.
Example Libghostty Projects > Adding a New Example

## Adding a New Example

1. Copy an existing example directory (e.g., `c-vt-encode-focus/`) as a
   starting point.
2. Update `build.zig.zon`: change `.name`, generate a **new unique**
   `.fingerprint` value (a random `u64` hex literal), and keep
   `.minimum_zig_version` matching the others.
3. Update `build.zig`: change the executable `.name` to match the directory.
4. Write a `README.md` following the existing format.
Example Libghostty Projects > Doxygen Snippet Tags

## Doxygen Snippet Tags

Example source files use Doxygen `@snippet` tags so the corresponding
header in `include/ghostty/vt/` can reference them. Wrap the relevant
code with `//! [snippet-name]` markers:

```c
//! [my-snippet]
int main() { ... }
//! [my-snippet]
```

The header then uses `@snippet <dir>/src/main.c my-snippet` instead of
inline `@code` blocks. Never duplicate example code inline in the
headers — always use `@snippet`. When modifying example code, keep the
snippet markers in sync with the headers in `include/ghostty/vt/`.

## Conventions

- Executable names use underscores: `c_vt_encode_focus` (not hyphens).
- All C examples link `ghostty-vt` via `lazyDependency("ghostty", ...)`.
- `build.zig` files follow a common template — keep them consistent.

@mainpage libghostty-vt - Virtual Terminal Emulator Library — libghostty-vt is a C library which implements a modern terminal emulator, extracted from the [Ghostty](https://ghostty.org) terminal emulator. libghostty-vt contains the logic for handling the core parts of a terminal

@file Color types and utilities.

# macOS Ghostty Application

- Use `swiftlint` for formatting and linting Swift code.
- If code outside of `macos/` directory is modified, use
  `zig build -Demit-macos-app=false` before building the macOS app to update
  the underlying Ghostty library.
- Use `macos/build.nu` to build the macOS app, do not use `zig build`
  (except to build the underlying library as mentioned above).
  - Build: `macos/build.nu [--scheme Ghostty] [--configuration Debug] [--action build]`
  - Output: `macos/build/<configuration>/Ghostty.app` (e.g. `macos/build/Debug/Ghostty.app`)
- Run unit tests directly with `macos/build.nu --action test`

## AppleScript

- The AppleScript scripting definition is in `macos/Ghostty.sdef`.
- Guard AppleScript entry points and object accessors with the
  `macos-applescript` configuration (use `NSApp.isAppleScriptEnabled`
  and `NSApp.validateScript(command:)` where applicable).
- In `macos/Ghostty.sdef`, keep top-level definitions in this order:
  1. Classes
  2. Records
  3. Enums
  4. Commands
- Test AppleScript support:
  (1) Build with `macos/build.nu`
  (2) Launch and activate the app via osascript using the absolute path
      to the built app bundle:
      `osascript -e 'tell application "<absolute path to build/Debug/Ghostty.app>" to activate'`
  (3) Wait a few seconds for the app to fully launch and open a terminal.
  (4) Run test scripts with `osascript`, always targeting the app by
      its absolute path (not by name) to avoid calling the wrong
      application.
  (5) When done, quit via:
      `osascript -e 'tell application "<absolute path to build/Debug/Ghostty.app>" to quit'`

Command launches sub-processes. This is an alternate implementation to the
Zig std.process.Child since at the time of authoring this, std.process.Child
didn't support the options necessary to spawn a shell attached to a pty.

Consequently, I didn't implement a lot of features that std.process.Child
supports because we didn't need them. Cross-platform subprocessing is not
a trivial thing to implement (I've done it in three separate languages now)
so if we want to replatform onto std.process.Child I'd love to do that.
This was just the fastest way to get something built.

Issues with std.process.Child:

* No pre_exec callback for logic after fork but before exec.
* posix_spawn is used for Mac, but doesn't support the necessary
features for tty setup.

TODO: This may have changed a lot now with the new I/O implementations in
>= 0.16.0, so this might warrant a recheck.

Surface represents a single terminal "surface". A terminal surface is
a minimal "widget" where the terminal is drawn and responds to events
such as keyboard and mouse. Each surface also creates and owns its pty
session.

The word "surface" is used because it is left to the higher level
application runtime to determine if the surface is a window, a tab,
a split, a preview pane in a larger window, etc. This struct doesn't care:
it just draws and responds to events. The events come from the application
runtime so the runtime can determine when and how those are delivered
(i.e. with focus, without focus, and so on).

"apprt" is the "application runtime" package. This abstracts the
application runtime and lifecycle management such as creating windows,
getting user input (mouse/keyboard), etc.

This enables compile-time interfaces to be built to swap out the underlying
application runtime. For example: pure macOS Cocoa, GTK+, browser, etc.

The goal is to have different implementations share as much of the core
logic as possible, and to only reach out to platform-specific implementation
code when absolutely necessary.

The periodic work of the GX layer on GTK windows (fork patch GX-0016),
on one timer for the whole application:

- herdr app mode. While the only tab of a window runs herdr (see
`src/gx/app_mode.zig`) and `gx-herdr-app-mode` is on,
`Window.getTabsVisible` hides the tab bar, so herdr looks like a
standalone application. With `gtk-titlebar-style = tabs` the tab bar
also holds the window controls, the new tab button and the main menu,
so `Window.getHeaderbarVisible` shows the header bar in its place and
the window stays usable. A window enters app mode once two checks in
a row find herdr (`gx.app_mode.State`) and leaves it at the first
check that does not.
- Unread marks. A tab that is not shown gets `needs-attention` when one
of its terminals prints something new (`gx.unread`); libadwaita draws
a line under the tab, and selecting the tab clears it.
- The kind of program in the foreground (`gx.leader`). A tab running a
remote session, a superuser shell or a container shows an icon, and
the window has the `gx-remote` or `gx-superuser` style class while
its selected tab runs one of the first two.

Checking the programs reads the name of each terminal's foreground
process, and lists the processes (one `gx.proc.Shared` table for every
window) only when that name is neither herdr nor a shell. Checks run
`gx.app_mode.min_delay_ms` after a terminal title change, a key press,
a tab or split change, a window shown or activated, or a configuration
change. While a window with a single tab has herdr app mode enabled,
they repeat at `gx.app_mode.nextDelay`, backing off to every 10 s while
nothing changes, and stop once herdr is confirmed. Disabled app mode
needs no timer; program icons follow events. Unread checks run every second while a
window has several tabs. Hidden, minimized and suspended windows are
skipped, and the timer stops when no shown window needs it.

Progress reports on tabs are in `progress.zig`.

Configuration errors are reported once (fork patch GX-0028).

Upstream `Application.showConfigErrorsDialog` runs for every
configuration change of the app and shows the configuration errors
dialog again while the configuration has diagnostics: a dismissed dialog
comes back, and an open one is presented again, which raises it and
takes the keyboard focus. Ghostty GX changes the configuration far more
often than a user edits it: each step of a theme preview in the settings
dialog, each saved setting (which reloads the files), a UI language
switch and a light or dark switch of the system. With an error in the
user's files, browsing themes with the arrow keys would bring the dialog
back on every step and move the focus away from the theme list.

`Reports` remembers the diagnostics the app reported, by their digest
(`gx.config_layers.diagnosticsDigest`), so the dialog only appears, or
comes to the front, for diagnostics not reported before: a reload that
keeps the same errors does not report them again. A configuration
without diagnostics clears the record, so the same errors made again
later are reported. The dialog's own Reload Configuration button clears
it too: the errors that are still there after that reload are shown
again rather than the dialog just going away.

Diagnostics only count as reported once a terminal window is shown.
Startup presents the dialog before there is any window, without a
parent, so it gets a window of its own that the first terminal window
then covers; upstream only brings it to the front at the next
configuration change, by presenting it again. `windowShown` tells the
app to show those diagnostics in the first window instead.

  fn windowShown(self: *Reports) bool — Records that a terminal window is shown.
  fn forget(self: *Reports) void — Lets the next diagnostics be shown even if they were reported before.

The Ghostty GX UI language on the GTK apprt: applies the `language`
configuration to gettext (the upstream GTK strings) and to `gx.i18n`
(the Ghostty GX strings), at startup and when it changes at runtime.

The language picks the gettext catalogs through `LANGUAGE`. glibc
ignores `LANGUAGE` while the messages locale is `C`, `POSIX` or
`C.UTF-8` (the WSL default), so the messages locale is switched to the
UTF-8 locale of the language when it is installed, else kept if it is
already a real locale, else set to the locale of another supported
language. Without any such locale only the `gx.i18n` strings follow the
language.

Pango picks the fonts for Han characters, which Chinese, Japanese and
Korean write differently, by the first language of `PANGO_LANGUAGE` or
`LANGUAGE` that uses them. Switching `LANGUAGE` would lose the system's
preference, so `PANGO_LANGUAGE` (unless set) lists the UI language
followed by the language Ghostty was started with. Child processes get
the original `LANG`, `LANGUAGE` and `PANGO_LANGUAGE` back (see
`restoreChildEnv`). `hanGlyphAvailable` tells whether any font can show
the Chinese UI at all.

The Ghostty GX settings dialog (fork patch GX-0015): the settings of
`src/gx/settings_map.zig` in an `Adw.PreferencesDialog`. Every change
is saved to the settings overlay `gui-settings.ghostty` (never to the
user's configuration file) and applied without the "Reloaded the
configuration" toast; changes made in quick succession are saved
together, and the dialog says when they are saved. A save that fails
keeps the changes and offers to try again. "Reset to Default" removes
the setting from the overlay (`settings_map.Changes.reset`), and every
row shows the value the applied configuration has.

The themes are listed on a subpage. Moving through the list previews
each theme: the configuration is built in memory from a snapshot of
the configuration layers (`gx.config_layers.Layers`) with a `--theme`
override. Applying a theme saves it; reverting, going back or closing
the dialog without applying ends the preview. A configuration that
follows the system's light or dark mode with two themes shows a row
for each.

The text is translated with the Ghostty GX tables (`src/gx/i18n.zig`,
not gettext) into the language of the configuration, and follows it
when it changes while the dialog is open. Without the Ghostty GX
layers (`GHOSTTY_GX_DEFAULTS=0`) the overlay is not loaded, so the
settings are shown but cannot be changed.

Quick Terminal: a borderless, topmost popup window with one tab
that slides in from an edge of a monitor (`quick-terminal-position`,
`quick-terminal-screen`) and out again. Owned by App, separate from the
normal windows list.

Showing (`toggle`, `present`): the window is placed on its monitor and
shown there cloaked, so it takes that monitor's DPI and its terminal
presents a frame before anything is seen (at most
`Window.first_frame_timeout_ms`). It takes the keyboard at once, so
what is typed right after the hotkey goes to the terminal. Then it
slides in from beyond its edge (centered: from a short way above).

Slides follow the time, one step per composed frame (`anim` clock): in
with `motion.enter` (decelerating), out with `motion.exit`
(accelerating); toggled midway, a slide turns around where it is
(`Slide.from`). While the window reaches onto another monitor or the
taskbar, a window region clips it to the work area. Without animations
(`anim.enabled`, `quick-terminal-animation-duration = 0`) it appears
and goes at once.

Hiding: hidden by the user while it has the keyboard, the quick
terminal hands the keyboard back to the window that had it before as
the slide starts. Its terminal stops rendering and the terminal's
popups (find bar, scrollbar, link preview) hide then too; the window's
other popups hide with it. With `quick-terminal-autohide` it slides out
when another window is activated, except its own popups and dialogs.

Sizes (`quick-terminal-size`, `sizeFor`) are DIPs of the target
monitor: `px` values and the defaults follow its DPI, percentages its
work area. Along an edge, a window shorter than the edge is centered on
it.

Themed scrollbar for the Win32 apprt: a layered popup owned by the
surface window that follows the system scrollbar mode ("Always show
scrollbars" in the accessibility settings). Being a top-level window,
the popup receives the WM_SETTINGCHANGE broadcast that announces a mode
change (the terminal's child window does not). `scrollbar = never`
turns it off (`setEnabled`).

The thumb is a thin rounded bar in the terminal's foreground color,
drawn translucent so it blends with any theme: 3 DIPs wide at rest,
widening to 8 and brightening while the pointer is over the scrollbar
or it is dragged. There is no thumb while everything fits
(`scrollable`). With always-visible scrollbars it reserves a column of
the grid and stays. In overlay mode (the default) it floats over the
terminal's right edge, hidden until there is something to scroll and
the user moves the viewport (`userScrolled`; reports never reveal it) or
rests the pointer on that edge (`onOwnerMouseMove`), and fades out
after a second without use. The fades and the widening run on the
`anim` frame clock and jump to their end when animations are off.

The pointer on the scrollbar: the wheel scrolls the terminal, dragging
the thumb scrolls along, a short track click jumps on release, and a
held press pages toward the pointer until the thumb gets there.
Shift+press jumps immediately and continues as a drag.

The popup is painted only when what it shows changed (`PaintKey`), into
a DIB kept while it is shown; moving the window only moves it, the fades
only change its opacity, and nothing is done for a hidden scrollbar
until it shows (background tabs, minimized windows, an overlay
scrollbar at rest).

Win32 Surface. Each Surface corresponds to one child HWND whose
private device context the renderer draws to with OpenGL (WGL).

The Surface translates Win32 input (keys, IME, mouse, drops) for the
core surface, implements the apprt surface callbacks (clipboard,
title, cursor) and orchestrates its popups: `ui/Palette.zig`
(`palette`), `ui/SearchBar.zig` (`search_bar`), `ui/LinkPreview.zig`
(`link_preview`), the context menu in `ui/Menu.zig` and the
confirmations in `ui/Dialogs.zig`.

Clipboard access that another application blocks is retried from
timers; dropped and pasted files are quoted for the shell running in
the terminal (`gx.path_quote`). The renderer thread reports frames
(`signalFrameDrawn`) and GPU resets (`gpuContextReset`) back here, and
reads the unfocused dim (`unfocusedDim`), bell border (`bellBorder`)
and client size (`clientSize`) that the GUI thread publishes in atomics.

Win32 Window. Each Window is a top-level container HWND that owns
one or more Surface child HWNDs as tabs (each tab a split tree).

The Window owns the tab model (split trees, active surfaces, titles,
unread and bell flags, the progress its terminals report, when each tab
was last selected), split layout and window-level state (DPI scale, size
limits, placement) and orchestrates the chrome modules. A tab shows its
title override (`set_tab_title`, renaming) or else the title of its
focused split (`refreshTabTitle`); the focused split is the one that
last got the keyboard focus (`setActiveSurface`). The tab bar reads
the rest of a tab's state from `tabStatus`. The chrome modules:

- `chrome/TitleBar.zig` (`title_bar`): non-client frame, the
integrated title bar row (caption buttons, main menu button,
tooltip), fullscreen and decorations; gets the first look at every
message and paints the chrome row.
- `chrome/TabBar.zig` (`tab_bar`): the tabs in that row: painting,
hit-testing, drag, context menu, inline rename, unread badges.
- `chrome/Backdrop.zig`: DWM theme, border, material, opacity, blur.
- `ui/ResizeOverlay.zig` (`resize_overlay`): the size overlay.
- `ui/ShortcutNotice.zig` (`shortcut_notice`): the notice about
shortcuts other programs take.
- `ui/Notice.zig` (`notice`) and `ui/Toast.zig` (`toast`): the
window's notice and toast at the bottom of the terminals
(`showNotice`, `showToast`).
- `ui/Menu.zig`: the main menu, opened through `queueMainMenu`.

The system broadcasts top-level windows get (settings, system colors,
visual style, accent color) go to `onSystemSettingChange`, which passes
them on to the design tokens, the app, the backdrop and the title bar.

Closing tabs (`closeTabByIndex`, `closeOtherTabs`, `closeTabsRightOf`,
the `close_tab` action) and the window (WM_CLOSE) asks first only when
a terminal runs a program (core `needsConfirmQuit`). herdr app mode
(`updateAppMode`) hides the tab bar while the only tab runs herdr.

The chrome is a single row at the top of the client area
(`chromeHeight`); the terminals fill the rest. A new window is placed
at about 80% of the work area of the monitor under the cursor
(cascading from other windows) unless `window-position-*` or
`window-width`/`window-height` say otherwise, and stays cloaked until
its first terminal frame is presented (at most `first_frame_timeout_ms`)
so it never flashes an unpainted frame.

Language changes reach the window through `onLanguageChanged`, DPI
changes through `WM_DPICHANGED` and configuration changes through
`onConfigChange`.

DPI (per-monitor v2, `dist/windows/ghostty.manifest`): only top-level
windows get WM_DPICHANGED. `handleDpiChange` rescales the chrome, gives
the active tab's surfaces the new content scale (`Surface.handleDpiChange`),
leaving hidden tabs to follow when selected (`applyScale`). It adopts
the rect Windows suggests and lays the panes out once. The popups are
top-level windows themselves: they get their own WM_DPICHANGED when

DWM chrome theming and window backdrop of a top-level terminal window:
the dark/light frame (`window-theme`, `background`), the border color,
the dark theme of common controls, the system backdrop material
(`gx-window-material`), translucency (`background-opacity`) and the
accent blur behind translucent windows (`background-blur`).

Materials: `mica`, `acrylic` and `tabbed` set `DWMWA_SYSTEMBACKDROP_TYPE`
(Windows 11 22H2, build 22621, and later; older systems fall back to
`solid` and log it). `extendFrame` extends the frame over the title bar
row, which `TitleBar` draws with per-pixel alpha (the strip and inactive
tabs show the material; active tabs follow terminal opacity). DWM draws its caption
buttons in that row, so the title bar uses them instead of its
custom-drawn ones (`TitleBar.nativeButtons`).

Per-pixel translucency (`perPixel`): when the terminals present frames
with an alpha channel DWM can use (`alphaFramesSupported`: build 22621
or later and the system OpenGL driver with an alpha pixel format) and
the window has a material or a `background-opacity` below one, the
window enables DWM blur-behind with an empty region
(`DwmEnableBlurBehindWindow`), which blurs nothing but makes DWM compose
the whole client area, the WGL child windows included, with the alpha
of its pixels. The renderers write premultiplied alpha: the terminal
background has `background-opacity`, glyphs, cursor, selection and
images stay opaque, and the material or the desktop shows through the
background only. GDI writes no alpha, so everything the window paints
itself goes through premultiplied 32bpp DIBs (`fillBackground`,
`fillOpaque`, the title bar). Without a material the desktop shows
through, blurred with `background-blur`.

Fallback (Windows 10 and builds before 22621, the Mesa software
renderer, a pixel format without alpha): the material shows in the
chrome only and `background-opacity` below one makes the whole window,
chrome and text included, uniformly translucent with `WS_EX_LAYERED`.

The 1px Windows 11 border (`setBorder`) follows the frame and the
activation, which `TitleBar` knows: the theme's hairline while the
window is active, the system's own inactive border while it is not,
none for borderless windows; with "Show accent color on title bars and
window borders" on, the system draws it in both states.

The state lives on the HWND; the DWM attributes this module set are
remembered per window (`applied`), so a configuration change that keeps
them (a theme preview step) makes no DWM call. `Window` calls `apply`
once after creating its HWND (it forgets what was remembered for that
HWND), `onConfigChange` after every app-level configuration change,
`onSystemSettingChange` for the system broadcasts and `extendFrame`
whenever the height of its chrome changes; `App` uses `toggleOpacity`
for `toggle_background_opacity` in the fallback.

The tab bar of a top-level terminal window: the tabs inside the chrome
row of `chrome/TitleBar.zig`, painted with Direct2D (8 DIP rounded top
corners; the active tab has the terminal background and flows into the
terminal below), hit-testing, hover, drag-to-reorder, the per-tab close
button, the tab status (progress, bell, new output, zoom), the new-tab
and launch profile buttons, the right-click menu, middle-click close and
inline renaming of tab and window titles.

The tab model (split trees, active surfaces, titles, unread and bell
flags, progress; the status of a tab in `Window.tabStatus`) stays in
`Window`; the tab bar reads it and asks the window to change it
(`selectTabIndex`, `closeTabByIndex`, `moveTabTo`, ...). The geometry
comes from the title bar `Layout` on demand (`geometry`,
`chrome/tab_layout.zig`), so hit tests never depend on a previous paint:
equal widths down to a minimum, the active tab with a floor and its
close button, inactive tabs with theirs while hovered; tabs that do not
fit scroll (wheel, scroll buttons, the active tab scrolled into view)
and a button lists them all (`Menu.showTabList`). Closing a tab with its
close button or the middle button keeps the widths until the pointer
leaves the tabs. In a maximized or fullscreen window the tabs take
clicks up to the screen edge.

Labels (`tab_layout.label`): an idle shell shows its title, a running
program `program · title` with the program in the secondary color. Every
two seconds one process table, shared by all windows (`App.processTable`,
one capture per period), tells each tab's focused terminal what runs in
it (`gx.proc.Tree.program`), whether that is idle (`gx-idle-processes`)
and what kind it is (`gx.leader`: remote, superuser, container), shown
as an icon. New output in background tabs comes from `gx.unread.Tracker`
(a baseline when the tab is hidden, checked every second without waiting
for the terminal lock); the bell marks the tab separately
(`Window.ringTab`). The status is compared every second so a progress
report that went stale repaints.

Dragging a tab moves it with the pointer after 10 DIPs; the others slide
aside (`anim`), the drop moves it in the model, and Escape (a keyboard
hook of the GUI thread while dragging, the terminal keeps the focus) or a
lost capture puts it back.

Renaming a tab or the window opens a text field over the tab: a popup
with a text input (`Popup.Options.text_input`) shown from the message
loop. Enter or clicking elsewhere keeps the text, Escape cancels; an
empty text removes the title override. Without Direct2D the field is an
Edit control.

The owning `Window` embeds this struct as `tab_bar` and forwards the
chrome row input to it, mostly through `TitleBar`.

Title bar and non-client frame of a top-level terminal window.

With `window-decoration = auto` or `client` the window keeps its native
frame (resize borders, shadow, Snap, the system menu) but extends the
client area over the caption in `WM_NCCALCSIZE`: the top row of the
client area is the integrated title bar. It holds the tabs
(`chrome/TabBar.zig`), the main menu button and custom-drawn caption
buttons. `WM_NCHITTEST` reports the empty parts of the row as
`HTCAPTION` (drag, double-click maximize, right-click system menu), the
top edge as `HTTOP`, the caption buttons as `HTMINBUTTON`,
`HTMAXBUTTON` (Windows 11 shows the Snap Layouts flyout over it) and
`HTCLOSE`, and the tabs and buttons as `HTCLIENT`; the geometry is the
pure `chrome/caption_layout.zig`. A maximized window takes hits on the
tabs and the main menu button up to the screen edge (`Layout.hit_top`).
The caption buttons are handled through the non-client mouse messages
so DefWindowProc never draws its classic buttons over the row: they
show their own tooltips, look pressed only while the pressed button is
under the pointer, and fade out of their hover look. With a window
material the DWM frame extends under the row and DWM draws its own
caption buttons there; the title bar then leaves the caption buttons to
DWM (`nativeButtons`, `DwmDefWindowProc`) instead of drawing over them.

`server` keeps the system caption and puts a tab row below it, `none`
drops the caption row (borderless), fullscreen windows show a plain tab
row and quick terminals no chrome at all. `toggleDecorations` switches
between the configured frame and borderless at runtime. Without
Direct2D nothing of the row can be drawn: windows then keep the system
caption and no chrome row.

`paint` draws the chrome row with Direct2D into a 32bpp DIB kept between
paints (`d2d.DibTarget`), with per-pixel alpha, and blits the part the
paint covers (a hover change repaints one button): opaque with the
solid material, transparent where the DWM backdrop shows through
otherwise (`chrome/Backdrop.zig`, `paintColors`). The title bar also
owns the chrome tooltip (`ui/Tooltip.zig`), shared with the tab bar, and
opens the window menu and the main menu (`ui/Menu.zig`). The owning
`Window` embeds this struct as `title_bar`.

Activation: popups that keep the window painted as active while they
have the focus (`Popup.Options.keep_owner_active`) lock it
(`Popup.WM_GX_OWNER_ACTIVE_LOCK`): while a lock is held,
`WM_NCACTIVATE(FALSE)` leaves the glyphs, the tabs and DWM's frame
active. When the last lock goes, the window checks once the activation
settled (`WM_APP_SYNC_ACTIVATION`) whether it is really active. The
window border follows the activation (`Backdrop.setBorder`).

Sizes, fonts, icons, hit-test rectangles, the canvas DPI and the
tooltip follow the window's content scale (`Window.scale`), like the
terminals. Only what Windows and DWM draw themselves keeps the real DPI
…

what the window knows: the layout of the row (`compute`) from the client
width, the row height, the frame, whether the window is maximized, its
content scale (`Window.scale`), the top resize band and where DWM draws

the smallest window the row fits in (`minTrackSize`), which `Window`
reports in `WM_GETMINMAXINFO`. `chrome/TitleBar.zig` gathers the inputs
from the window. Only depends on `std` and `win32.RECT`.

Tab bar geometry and labels that need no window: where the tabs and the
buttons of a window's tab strip go (`compute`), which slot a dragged tab
lands in (`dragTarget`, `dragSlotLeft`), the text a tab shows (`label`)
and the stored BGRA fill of an active tab that joins a translucent
terminal (`backgroundPixel`). `chrome/TabBar.zig` paints and hit-tests with
them. Color math is shared with `Backdrop` through `alpha.zig`.

The tabs share the strip in equal widths from `max_width` down to
`min_width`; the active tab keeps at least `active_min_width`, enough for
its close button and some text. When even that does not fit, the tabs
keep those widths and scroll between two scroll buttons, with a button
listing every tab after them. After a tab closed through its close
button the widths stay (`Frozen`) until the pointer leaves the strip, so
the next close button lands under the pointer.

The Windows clipboard for the terminals, dialogs and popup text inputs.

Another application can hold the clipboard open for a moment (clipboard
managers, remote desktop tools such as RustDesk or ToDesk syncing it),
and `OpenClipboard` fails meanwhile, so `open` tries a few times with a
short pause in between, as Windows Terminal does. The pauses block the
calling (GUI) thread: `attempts` and `retry_delay_ms` keep that short,
and callers that can wait longer retry from a timer (`Surface`).

"HTML Format" (`htmlDocument`); text read back is bounded by the size of
its memory block and decoded leniently (`unicodeText`).

GUI-thread launcher for the medium-integrity drop receiver (DropCompanion).
The elevated terminal cannot receive drops from normal-privilege windows
(UIPI), so it opens a separate normal-privilege receiver. This is a standard
same-user de-elevation: it duplicates the primary token of the desktop shell
(GetShellWindow) and starts the receiver with it via CreateProcessWithTokenW.
The elevated token's own TokenLinkedToken cannot be used: outside SYSTEM it
is an identification-level token, which fails with
ERROR_BAD_IMPERSONATION_LEVEL (1346). It is still read, to prove that the
shell token is exactly this elevated token's limited half: same user SID and
session, Limited/medium/not elevated, and the shell's logon session equal to
the linked AuthenticationId. Every fact comes from a process or token handle
held for the whole check, never from a PID alone.
It never bypasses UAC, never relaxes a UIPI message filter, and never falls
back to a privileged launch (runas / high CreateProcess). On any failure it
returns a distinct Outcome so the caller can explain why nothing opened.

Keyboard shortcuts that never reach Ghostty GX: chords another program
registered as a global hotkey (RegisterHotKey) and the preserved keys
of the active input method (TSF). Windows hands neither to the focused
window.

`App` probes the configured keybindings after the first window is up
and after every configuration reload: `candidates` lists the first
chord of each binding that has a modifier, without Ghostty GX's own
`global:` hotkeys and the chords Windows reserves but still delivers
(Alt+F4, the F12 debugger keys); `probe` registers each one on the
message-only window and unregisters it at once, where
ERROR_HOTKEY_ALREADY_REGISTERED means another program holds it, and
asks the GUI thread's TSF keystroke manager for the input method's
preserved keys (`ITfKeystrokeMgr::GetPreservedKey`). An input method
registers those only once it is active on the thread, and keys its
keystroke sink eats are not among them: Microsoft Pinyin's
Ctrl+Shift+F (simplified/traditional) is not a preserved key, so it is
not found.

The results (`Conflicts`) mark the bindings in the keyboard shortcut
sheet, keep their hints out of the menus (`ui/trigger.zig::Hints`) and
decide the one-time notice (`noticeBindings`, `ui/ShortcutNotice.zig`).

Modal dialogs of the win32 apprt: confirmations (closing a terminal,
tabs or a window with running processes, quitting, clipboard access,
unsafe paste), notices (child exited, About) and the native Save As
dialog.

Every function blocks in a modal loop and returns the user's choice.
The modal loop keeps dispatching messages, so callers must not use
pointers that a dispatched message can free (a surface whose child
exits, for example) after the call; re-resolve them instead. Core
callbacks must post their request to the message loop before calling
this module. Terminals and windows hold back their WM_CLOSE while a
dialog is open (`deferClose`); it is re-posted when the outermost
dialog returns.

The dialogs are drawn in the colors of the terminal theme on a `Popup`
owned by the window, centered on it and laid out at its content scale
(`Window.scale`): an icon and a title, the body text, optionally the
running processes (by tab), a preview of clipboard text
(`previewLines`: line ends, control and invisible characters made
visible), links, a check box, and a row of `controls` buttons with the
default one in the accent color. They are task modal: every other
window of the app is disabled while a dialog is open, and dialogs
opened from inside a dialog nest. Enter activates the focused button
(initially the default button, which is Cancel for anything
destructive), Tab, Shift+Tab and the arrow keys move the focus and show
the focus ring, Space activates it, Escape and Alt+F4 cancel and Ctrl+C
copies the text. A close sent to the dialog from outside (WM_CLOSE, the
system close) cancels too and gives the activation back to the window.

Without Direct2D, without a Ghostty window as owner, or while a screen
reader runs (`SPI_GETSCREENREADER`, or `GHOSTTY_GX_A11Y=screen-reader`),
the dialogs are native task dialogs (`TaskDialogIndirect`), and message
boxes where those are missing; their text is prepared the same way.

Text is translated with `gx.i18n` at call time.

The keyboard shortcut sheet: a large `Popup` centered on a window that
lists every keybinding of the configuration (`gx.shortcuts`) by
category in a fixed order, one row per action with its title in the UI
language, the action and the keycaps of every key sequence that runs it
(leader sequences as `A → B`, keys without a name such as media keys
last).

The search field filters by title (translated or English), action and
keys (`gx.shortcuts.Search`): a query written as keys (`ctrl+t`) matches
only those keys, and the rows of a category are ordered by score. Alt+K
or the Record Keys button records the keys pressed next into the field
as such a query (`"Ctrl+Shift+T"`); after a leader key the next key goes
on with its sequence; Escape or Alt+K stops recording.

Rows can be selected (Up, Down, Page Up, Page Down, Ctrl+Home, Ctrl+End
or a click); Enter or a double click closes the sheet and performs the
row's actions. Any other chord bound to an action closes the sheet and
performs it, the `gx:keybinds` chord just closes it; Home, End and the
editing chords stay with the search field.

A key sequence whose first chord another program or the input method
takes (`App.shortcut_conflicts`) has a warning marker, its row names
the taken keys on a second line, and a note at the top of the list
explains each reason once.

Opened by `gx:keybinds`, the main menu's Keyboard Shortcuts item and the
shortcut notice through `show`. The sheet of a window lives in the
command palette of the window's active terminal (`Palette.keybinds`), so
the terminal owns it. It lays out at the window's content scale
(`Window.scale`) and keeps the window painted as active
(`Popup.Options.keep_owner_active`). The keycaps are measured once when
the sheet opens and their text layouts are kept (`KeycapCache`), so
hovering and scrolling reuse their layouts.

While a screen reader runs (`SPI_GETSCREENREADER`, or
`GHOSTTY_GX_A11Y=screen-reader` for testing), or when Direct2D is not
available, a native TaskDialogIndirect lists and copies the shortcuts;
Windows keeps it inside its monitor's work area and scrolls a long
list. It is posted through `List` so its modal loop never runs in a core
callback; its text is copied before the loop. If the API is unavailable,
`List` shows a read-only edit control in the system colors instead.
Escape closes either native view.

The hovered-URL preview of a terminal surface: a small rounded bubble
at the bottom-left of the surface, like a browser status bubble, driven
by the `mouse_over_link` apprt action. It is a non-activating,
click-through `Popup` drawn with the `Canvas`, at most 60% as wide as
the surface: a longer URL keeps its scheme and host and loses the
middle of the rest (`elide`). While the pointer is over the bubble's
place it moves to the bottom-right corner (`placement`), so it never
covers the link. The same URL at the same place shows without new
work, and leaving a link hides the bubble after a short delay, so
moving between links does not flicker.

A `Surface` embeds this struct as `link_preview` and calls `show`; the
runtime UI of a remote pane (`RemoteRuntimeUi.zig`) embeds one and
calls `showRemote` with the pane, which has no `Surface`. Both call
`hide` and `deinit`. A show places the bubble on the terminal's own
child window (`Host`), colors it from that terminal's app and creates
the popup again for another window (the tab moved) or the other dark
or light frame (`Palette.ensurePopup`).

Context and application menus of the win32 apprt, drawn and run by
`ui/MenuPopup.zig` (native menus for screen readers and without
Direct2D, `MenuPopup.runNative`).

Each `show*` function builds its menu on demand and runs it modally at
an anchor: the main menu below the main menu button, lined up with its
right edge (also from the keyboard); the launch profile menu below the
new-tab button; the window menu, the context menus and the list of all
tabs where they are asked for. The context menus return what the user
picked (null when the menu was dismissed) and the caller performs the
choice, the tab bar with `performTabCommand`; the other menus perform
the picked item themselves, the window menu by posting its
`WM_SYSCOMMAND`. Because menus are built on every invocation they always
use the current UI language (labels are English msgids translated with
`gx.i18n.tr`, with access keys from the English labels); a menu that is
open while the language switches closes (`onLanguageChanged`).

A menu runs a modal loop that keeps dispatching messages, so call it
from a window message (e.g. a click), never from a core callback; key
bindings go through `Window.queueMainMenu`, `queueNewTabMenu` and
`queueContextMenu`. One menu is open at a time. A menu whose owner
window or terminal went away while it was open returns null, and the
menus perform the pick only while their window is still open.

A custom-drawn popup menu in the Windows 11 style, themed from the
terminal colors (`style.Tokens`): the widget behind `ui/Menu.zig`. Each
open menu level is a `Popup` window painted with a `d2d.Canvas`, laid
out on whole device pixels: rows with an optional icon (or emoji) or a
check/radio mark, a label, right-aligned shortcut text and a submenu
chevron, separators, section headers and disabled items. The
highlighted row gets the hover fill; a row highlighted from the
keyboard also gets the accent selection indicator.

Build the items with a `Builder` and `run` them. `run` opens the menu
below an anchor rectangle (a point is an empty one, `Options.at`), lined
up with its left or right edge (`Options.alignment`), above the anchor
or flipped to its other edge when it does not fit (`placeRoot`), within
the work area of the anchor's monitor and sized for the owner's DPI (or
the content scale in `Options.owner_scale`). A menu taller than the
work area scrolls: the wheel, the keyboard, and the arrow strips at its
ends, which scroll while the pointer rests on them. `run` blocks in a
modal message loop until an action is picked (its `Item.id` is
returned) or the menu is dismissed (null). The popups of one run are
created once per level and reused for every submenu shown at that
level; `Popup.show` keeps a popup cloaked until it has painted. Only the
root's DC canvas and DIB may survive for three seconds between runs;
no window, callback, menu model or text layout stays in that cache.

Like a native menu, the menu takes neither activation nor keyboard
focus. The loop handles the keyboard itself on the deepest open menu:
Up/Down, Home/End, Page Up/Page Down, Enter/Space, Right to open and
Left to close a submenu, Escape, Alt/F10, and access keys (`Item.access`,
else a letter or digit of the label): the key is underlined in its
label while access keys are shown (opened from the keyboard, a key was
pressed, or the system always underlines them), and a label without it
(a translation) shows it as "(T)" when the menu was opened from the
keyboard. A key an input method takes (`VK_PROCESSKEY`) is read back
with `ImmGetVirtualKey`, and its composition is canceled when the menu
uses the key. Keys that were down when the menu opened do nothing while
they stay down (their auto-repeat), and their releases go on to the
focused window, which saw them go down.

The mouse is routed by screen position while the root popup holds the
mouse capture: hovering a submenu item opens it after the system menu
show delay; while the pointer heads for an open submenu across other
rows of its parent (`inAimTriangle`), the parent keeps its highlight;
a parent menu always highlights the item whose submenu the pointer or
the keyboard is in (`highlightPath`). A press outside the menus, losing
the capture, hiding or minimizing its owner, or a change of the
foreground window dismisses the menu.
Releasing a button over an item picks it when a button went down inside

A notice at the bottom of a window, after the WinUI InfoBar: a severity
(accent, success, caution or critical color with its icon), a title, a
body, up to two action buttons and a close button. It generalizes
`ShortcutNotice` for the configuration errors, reload results, child
process exits and key state hints of the app.

It never takes the focus or Escape, pauses its timeout while the
pointer is over it (and gives 5 more seconds after), lasts at least the
system's notification time (`SPI_GETMESSAGEDURATION`), fades in over
167 ms (`Popup.Options.motion`) and waits while a modal dialog has its
window disabled. Hidden or moving Quick owners defer feedback until
their next settled show; closing owners discard it. Deadlines reject
queued old timeout messages. Key names stay on one line (`glueChord`).

Usage: embed a `Notice` in an address-stable owner (the window); call
`show` from the message loop, or `post` from a core callback (it shows
from the message loop, through `WM_SHOW_POSTED` on its own popup
window), with a `Placement` (the window, its terminal area and scale)
and `Content`. Move it with `reposition`, close it with `hide` and free
it with `deinit`. `Callbacks` report the action chosen and why it
closed. Timers `NT` (timeout) and `NW` (waiting for a dialog) live on
the notice's popup window.

The command palette of a terminal surface: a `Popup` centered near the
top of its window, with a filter input (IME-capable) over a scrollable
list and a footer that describes the selected entry and the keys that
act on it. It has pages (`Page`):

- the root lists the recently used entries, the window's other tabs
("Switch to Tab: <title>"), the configured `command-palette-entry`
commands with the keycaps of their bindings, the settings sections
(`Settings.showSection`) and the UI language. "New Tab…" and "Change
Theme…" open the next two pages; a filter also finds their entries;
- "New Tab…" lists the launch profiles (like `gx:new_tab_profile`);
Ctrl+Enter opens one in a new window;
- "Change Theme…" lists the themes with their colors. While the
selection rests on a theme the terminals preview it, and leaving the
page or closing the palette without picking one restores the saved
theme. The page opens on the current theme and previews nothing
until the user moves the selection or types. Enter saves the theme
to `gui-settings.ghostty` and closes the palette, Shift+Enter keeps
it open;
- the tab switcher (`toggle(.tabs)`, for `toggle_tab_overview` and
`gx:tab_switcher`) lists the window's tabs, the most recently used
first, with the previous one selected.

Backspace in an empty filter goes back to the root. Entries match
(`gx.fuzzy`: words in any order, pinyin initials) in the UI language and
in English, also while an input method composes; when nothing matches,
the filter is tried again with two neighboring characters swapped. The
matched characters are highlighted, and an entry found by its English
title shows that title on a second line. Matches are grouped, the groups
ordered by their best match (`palette_model.sortMatches`).

Picks are kept between runs (`gx.palette_history`, in the state file),
keyed by the English msgid, action or theme name: the recently used
entries come first in the root and rank higher in filtered results,
and the entry picked most after typing the same text comes first.
Shift+Delete forgets the selected entry, "Clear Recently Used" all.

The owning `Window` embeds this struct as `palette` and calls
`setActive` (from `toggle_command_palette`), `reposition` (on resize),
`onDpiChanged`, `onLanguageChanged` and `deinit`. The app's message
loop gives `handleKey` the first look at key presses in the popup
(`ownsEdit`); chords bound to other actions then bubble up to the
surface, and editing chords stay with the filter (`text_edit`). The
palette also hosts the window's keyboard shortcut sheet (`keybinds`,
see `Keybinds.zig`), which shares its lifetime.

Reusable owned popup host for custom-drawn UI (link preview, command
palette, menus, flyouts): a `WS_POPUP` window owned by a terminal
window, with Windows 11 rounded corners (`DWMWA_WINDOW_CORNER_PREFERENCE`)
and the system drop shadow, per-monitor DPI, Direct2D rendering through
a `d2d.Canvas`, keyboard, mouse (hover/click/wheel) and an optional
IME-capable single-line text input for filter boxes.

Usage: embed a `Popup` in an address-stable owner struct, `create` it
once with `Callbacks` (paint, key, mouse, text, dismissed), position it
with `show(rect)` (screen pixels; size content in DIPs with `scale`),
repaint with `invalidate`, and `destroy` it with the owner. Dismissal
(Escape, click outside, lost activation) hides the popup and reports
the reason through `Callbacks.dismissed`. A popup that belongs to a
window's chrome follows the window's content scale (`setOwnerScale`);
`applyTheme` follows a theme change without a new window.

Lifecycle: `show` from hidden keeps the window cloaked until it painted
once (synchronously) and a frame passed (timer `RV`), so DWM never
shows it empty; `show` and `setBounds` leave an unchanged window alone.
WM_CLOSE (Alt+F4, the system close) hides a shown popup instead of
destroying it, reports `.owner` and, for an activating popup with
`Options.close_owner_on_close`, closes the window it belongs to; a
hidden popup ignores it. When Windows destroys the popup with its owner
(WM_NCDESTROY), `hwnd` becomes null and the render target goes; the
owner frees the rest with `destroy` or recreates it with `create`.
With `Options.keep_owner_active` an activating popup sends
`WM_GX_OWNER_ACTIVE_LOCK` (wparam 1) to its root owner before it takes
activation and (wparam 0) once it hid or lost activation, so the owner
can keep painting its frame as active; the owner re-evaluates its
frame on unlock. With `Options.motion` the popup fades in (`anim`, the
167 ms entrance of `gx.motion`) as a layered window painted through a
`d2d.DibTarget`.

Text input: with `Options.text_input` the popup keeps a `TextInput`
(`popup.input`) that receives typing, editing keys (`text_edit`: words,
undo, Shift+Insert/Ctrl+Insert/Shift+Delete), clipboard (a paste keeps
the field within `text_edit.max_len` code units), mouse selection and
IME composition; draw it with `drawTextInput` (or
`drawTextInputEx`) in the paint callback and read it with
`TextInput.text`. Keys go to `Callbacks.key` first, so owners can take
Up/Down/Enter before the input sees them. The caret blinks at the
system rate (timer `CB`) only while the popup has the keyboard focus,
and an invisible system caret follows it for magnifiers; the IME
candidate window is placed below the field (`CFS_EXCLUDE`) only while
composing. `Callbacks.composition_changed` reports the composition.

Owner timers and messages: `startRepeat` (timer `RP`) calls
`Callbacks.repeat` at the keyboard repeat rate while a button is held;
other timers set on the popup window go to `Callbacks.timer`, and

The find bar of a terminal surface: a rounded `Popup` at the top-right
of the surface with a search icon, an IME-capable needle input, the
"{current}/{total}" match counter and previous/next/close buttons with
tooltips (`ui/Tooltip.zig`), drawn in the theme colors. The bar takes
the surface width less its margins, between 240 and 380 DIPs
(`barWidth`), and the counter the width of its widest value for the
match count (`counterSizing`). Typing searches through the core
`search` binding action; Enter/Shift+Enter, F3/Shift+F3, the arrow keys
and the buttons navigate, and Escape or the close button ends the
search. When nothing matches, the field gets the caution border and
"No results" shows in the caution color at text contrast. The bar
stays open while the terminal has the focus, like the GTK and macOS
find bars (without its caret then), F3/Shift+F3 navigate from the
terminal too (performable bindings in `src/gx/defaults-windows.ghostty`),
and it hides with its surface (a background tab). Closing the bar any
way, Alt+F4 included, ends the search. Without Direct2D the bar cannot
open, and a message box says so.

resizes and window moves (`reposition`), its visibility
(`setOwnerVisible`), DPI changes, a move to another window
(`onReparented`) and `deinit`. The app's message loop gives keys typed
into the bar to `handleKey` first (see `App.run`, `ownsEdit`), then lets
keybindings with Ctrl reach the terminal, which takes the focus while
the bar stays open.

move between rows and through lists, Left/Right change a choice,
a switch, the font size or the button of a group, Enter and Space
activate, Delete resets the focused setting, PgUp/PgDn scroll, Esc
clears a filter box and then closes. The focus ring shows once the
keyboard moved the focus.

takes the typing while the list is focused (fuzzy matching,

filter box. Font families also match by their name in the user's

part it went down on; list items are picked on the press, and the

small steps and scrolls the lines `SPI_GETWHEELSCROLLLINES` asks for;

is read again; the snapshot follows the changes made here) and the rows

a value that comes from the configuration file or the command line says

configuration is built from the snapshot with an in-memory `--theme`

The frame clock of the custom-drawn UI: time-based `Tween`s, whether
to animate at all (`enabled`), and a clock that calls running
animations once per display refresh. The durations and easing curves
are the shared ones of `gx.motion` (re-exported as `motion`): Fluent's
83/167/250 ms, entering elements `motion.enter`, leaving ones
`motion.exit`, movements `motion.ease`.

The clock: while an `Animator` runs, a background thread waits for the
next DWM composition (`DwmFlush`) and posts one `WM_TICK` to a
message-only window of this module (class `GhosttyGxAnimClock`); the GUI
thread then calls every running animator. The next tick is posted only
after the GUI thread handled the previous one, so a busy GUI thread gets
fewer ticks rather than a queue of them, and without running animators
the thread sleeps on an event. The thread starts with the first
animation and is detached: it lives until the process exits. Animations
compute their progress from the elapsed time (`Tween`), so a late frame
skips ahead instead of slowing the animation down. The clock thread
follows the idea of Zed's Windows vsync thread (Apache-2.0, idea only):
DwmFlush in a loop, sleeping a refresh period when it returns at once.

`enabled` is `motion.enabled` for this system: the Windows "Animation
effects" setting (`SPI_GETCLIENTAREAANIMATION`), off in remote sessions
(`SM_REMOTESESSION`), and `GHOSTTY_GX_ANIMATIONS` (read once) overrides
both. Callers ask it when an animation would start and jump to the end
state when it says no.

Everything except the clock thread runs on the GUI thread.

  fn progress(self: Tween, now_ns: u64) f32 — The eased progress at `now_ns`, 0..1.
  fn done(self: Tween, now_ns: u64) bool
  fn lerp(self: Tween, now_ns: u64, from: f32, to: f32) f32 — The value between `from` and `to` at `now_ns`.

Hand-written Direct2D 1.1 and DirectWrite bindings for the win32 UI,
and `Canvas`, the drawing helper every custom-drawn surface (popups,
title bar, tab bar, settings) paints with.

Only the methods the UI calls are typed; the remaining vtable slots are
opaque placeholders that keep the layout (checked against the mingw-w64
d2d1.h / dwrite*.h vtables). Methods that return structs by value are
never called.

`Factory` holds the process-wide D2D/DirectWrite factories, the
resolved UI/icon/monospace font families (Segoe UI Variable in its
Small, Text and Display optical sizes when installed), the CJK font
fallback (chosen from the UI language and the user locale), a text
format cache and a cache of laid-out text (`TextCache`); the app owns
one (`App.uiFactory`), and a failed creation is logged and remembered
once. A `Canvas` belongs to one render target (an HWND or a GDI DC) and
draws in DIPs: 1 unit = 1 pixel at 96 DPI. HWND targets present without
waiting for the vertical blank; DC targets render in software (their
pixels go back to GDI anyway). `Canvas.snap*`, `hairline*` and
`strokeRoundedRectPx` put edges on device pixels so thin lines stay
sharp at 125 % and 150 %. `beginDib` separates coverage and glyph
rasterization from stored BGRA backgrounds: replacement keeps channels
above alpha in the terminal's linear-light storage contract.

Text: `drawText`/`measureText` lay out UTF-8 through the cache;
`TextLayout` is a layout the caller keeps, with hit testing, caret
positions and cluster stops for text inputs; `drawTextRuns` and
`drawLayout` color or embolden ranges (match highlights);
`drawTextMiddle` puts the ellipsis in the middle (paths).

All of it is single-threaded and must only be used on the GUI thread.

The dimmed backdrop behind the settings overlay: a black, translucent
(`WS_EX_LAYERED` with a constant alpha), non-activating popup that
covers the terminal window below the overlay. A click on it reports
through `Callbacks.click`, which closes the overlay like a click outside
a modal dialog. It fades in (`anim`, the entrance of `gx.motion`) and
has the rounded corners of the window unless the window is maximized
or full screen.

Show it before the overlay so the overlay stays on top of it; both are
owned by the terminal window. A close sent from outside (`taskkill`
without /F sends one to every window) leaves it alone: the overlay and
the window get their own. The backdrop also hears `WM_FONTCHANGE`, which
Windows broadcasts to top-level windows when fonts are installed or
removed (`Callbacks.font_change`).

fn create(self: *Scrim, hinstance: w32.HINSTANCE, owner: w32.HWND, alpha: u8, callbacks: Callbacks) !void — Create the (hidden) backdrop owned by `owner`, with `alpha` (0-255) of black.

fn isOwnWindow(hwnd: w32.HWND, owner_struct: *const anyopaque) bool — Whether `hwnd` is still the window created for `owner_struct`: it exists and carries its pointer (a destroyed window's handle can be reused).

Design tokens of the win32 UI: the colors (`Tokens`) and sizes in DIPs
(`space`, `radius`, `control`, `row`, `type_ramp`, `icon`,
`close_button`, `selection_indicator`, `focus_ring`; the older
`metrics` and `font_size` stay for existing callers), and the helpers
to scale them to pixels and to shade a fill for hover and press.
Spacing, radii and control, row and button sizes are multiples of 4
DIPs (checked at compile time); hairlines are one device pixel
(`d2d.Canvas.hairline`).

The colors come from the interface library the GTK app shares:
`gx.ui_tokens` derives them from the terminal colors with the color
math of `gx.ui_color` (contrast floors on every surface, the accent,
pressed fainter than hovered, the WinUI focus ring of a foreground
outer and a surface inner stroke), and `gx.chrome` the title bar strip,
its overlays, the window border and the caption close button. `Tokens`
carries both: every field of `gx.ui_tokens.Tokens` under the same name
(a comptime check keeps them in step) and the chrome colors the title
bar and tab bar draw. `Color` is `gx.ui_color.Color`. A theme is dark
when the gamma-encoded luma of its background is under one half
(`ui_color.isDark`); contrast ratios use WCAG luminance
(`ui_color.luminance`).

High contrast: while Windows high contrast is on (`system`),
`fromConfig` returns `fromSystem`, the system colors, with
`high_contrast` set so cards and inputs get borders. `system` is GUI
thread state read on first use; `System.refresh` reads it again, to be
called after WM_SETTINGCHANGE, WM_SYSCOLORCHANGE or WM_THEMECHANGED.

`fromConfig` caches the tokens of the last colors it saw (the color
values, not the config) on the GUI thread; call it when painting.

The editing model of the single-line text inputs of the custom-drawn
UI (`Popup.TextInput`): UTF-16 text with a caret and a selection
anchor, movement by character and by word, an undo history and the
editing keys of a Windows text box (Ctrl+arrows, Ctrl+Backspace and
Ctrl+Delete, Shift+Insert, Ctrl+Insert, Shift+Delete, Ctrl+Z/Y,
Alt+Backspace).

Pure functions without Win32 calls: `handleKey` reports clipboard keys
as a `Clipboard` intent and the caller moves the text (`deleteSelection`
after a cut, `paste` with the clipboard text, which keeps the field
within `max_len` code units). The functions take any struct with the
fields of `Text` (`buf`, `caret`, `anchor`, `history`), such as
`Popup.TextInput`.

Characters: the caret never lands inside a surrogate pair, and combining
marks, variation selectors, emoji modifiers, zero-width joiner sequences
and regional indicator pairs move with their base character (an
approximation of grapheme clusters, also for UTF-8 text with
`nextCharUtf8`; callers that laid the text out pass the DirectWrite
cluster stops instead). Words: a run of letters and
digits, a run of Han characters (Chinese has no spaces between words,
so a run of Hanzi counts as one word), a run of hiragana, katakana or
Hangul, or a run of punctuation; whitespace separates them.

The undo history follows stb_textedit (public domain): a bounded list of
replace records, consecutive typing and deleting merged into one step.

UTF-8 to NUL-terminated UTF-16 conversion for Win32 calls whose text is
only known at runtime (translated strings, titles, paths), and back, and
offsets between the two encodings (DirectWrite ranges are in UTF-16
code units). Both directions decode the same way: an invalid UTF-8 byte
or an unpaired surrogate becomes one U+FFFD.

fn utf16Len(text: []const u8) usize — The number of UTF-16 code units `bufZ` produces for `text`, without the terminator.
fn bufZ(buf: []u16, text: []const u8) [:0]const u16 — Convert `text` into `buf` and return the NUL-terminated result.
fn allocZ(alloc: Allocator, text: []const u8) Allocator.Error![:0]u16 — Convert `text` into a newly allocated NUL-terminated string.
fn truncate(units: []const u16, max_len: usize) []const u16 — The first `max_len` code units of `units` at most, without a high surrogate at the end that has lost (or never had) its low surrogate.
fn utf8Alloc(alloc: Allocator, units: []const u16) Allocator.Error![]u8 — Convert UTF-16 `units` into newly allocated UTF-8.
fn utf8Buf(buf: []u8, units: []const u16) []const u8 — Convert UTF-16 `units` into `buf` as UTF-8, like `utf8Alloc`; text that does not fit is cut at a codepoint boundary.
fn utf16Index(text: []const u8, byte_index: usize) usize — The UTF-16 offset of byte `byte_index` of UTF-8 `text`: the number of code units `bufZ` makes of `text[0..byte_index]`.
fn byteIndex(text: []const u8, unit_index: usize) usize — The byte offset in UTF-8 `text` of UTF-16 offset `unit_index`; an offset inside a surrogate pair maps to the start of its codepoint.

# Benchmarking

The benchmark tools are split into two roles:

- `ghostty-gen` generates synthetic input data.
- `ghostty-bench` consumes existing input data and runs a benchmark.

## Workflow

- For timing comparisons, generate data first and benchmark it later.
- Do not pipe `ghostty-gen` directly into `ghostty-bench` when comparing
  performance. That mixes generation cost into the measurement and makes
  branch-to-branch comparisons noisy.
- Reuse the exact same generated files when comparing revisions.
- Prefer deterministic generation inputs such as fixed seeds when the
  generator supports them.
- Keep large generated benchmark corpora outside the repository unless the
  change explicitly requires checked-in test data.

## Running Benchmarks

- Prefer `hyperfine` to compare benchmark timings.
- Benchmark the `ghostty-bench` command line, not the generator.
- Use `ghostty-bench ... --data <path>` with pre-generated files.
- Run multiple warmups and repeated measurements so branch comparisons are
  based on medians instead of single runs.
- When comparing branches, keep all benchmark inputs and CLI flags the same,
  including terminal dimensions.
- Never run multiple benchmarks in parallel on the same machine, as they will
  interfere with each other and produce unreliable results.

## Building

- Build benchmark tools with `zig build -Demit-bench -Doptimize=ReleaseFast`.
- On macOS, add `-Demit-macos-app=false` to avoid building the macOS app.
- Make sure you specify `-Doptimize=ReleaseFast` when building benchmarks,
  otherwise the debug build will be very slow and not representative of real
  performance.

## Comparing Branches

- When comparing branches, switch to that branch, build the binary, then
  rename it e.g. `zig-out/bin/ghostty-bench` to `zig-out/bin/ghostty-bench-branch1`.
  Replace branch1 with something better.
- Then switch to the other branch, build it, and rename it to
  `zig-out/bin/ghostty-bench-branch2`. Replace branch2 with something better.
- Then run all the benchmarks with `hyperfine` comparing the N binaries
  we want to.
